browser.expected422Classification: The two resource errors are the deliberate same-actor publish and reject requests used to prove separation of duties.

items.operation: Compare two published topology versions in the real topology detail drawer
items.verificationSql: SELECT topology_code,version,state,revision,definition FROM bpi.bpi_topology_versions WHERE topology_code LIKE 'ADP_E2E_20260718_023214_BPI_LIFECYCLE%';
items.evidence: The real drawer displayed a deterministic 11-item diff from 1.0.0 to 2.0.0, including /localityGroup and node/edge additions. Comparison is read-only; both source versions were queried directly before marker cleanup.

items.operation: Compare published and draft rule versions in the real rule detail drawer
items.verificationSql: SELECT rule_code,version,state,revision,definition FROM bpi.bpi_rule_versions WHERE rule_code LIKE 'ADP_E2E_20260718_023214_BPI_LIFECYCLE%';
items.evidence: The real drawer displayed the deterministic AST change at /conditions/0/threshold together with the topology reference change. Cross-code and cross-scope comparisons remain fail closed.

items.operation: Run bounded historical replay for the publish and reject candidates
items.verificationSql: SELECT r.rule_code,s.state,s.metrics,s.checksum FROM bpi.bpi_rule_simulations s JOIN bpi.bpi_rule_versions r ON r.id=s.rule_version_id WHERE r.rule_code LIKE 'ADP_E2E_20260718_023214_BPI_LIFECYCLE%';
items.evidence: Both POST requests returned 202. Both persisted simulations were PASSED with matched=1, missed=0, falsePositive=0 and meanBoundaryErrorSeconds=0; each rule advanced from DRAFT/r1 to SIMULATION_PASSED/r2.

items.operation: Submit the exact latest passed simulation for approval from the real rule drawer
items.verificationSql: SELECT r.rule_code,r.state,r.revision,a.state,a.simulation_id,a.submitted_by FROM bpi.bpi_rule_versions r JOIN bpi.bpi_rule_approval_requests a ON a.rule_version_id=r.id WHERE r.rule_code LIKE 'ADP_E2E_20260718_023214_BPI_LIFECYCLE%';
items.evidence: Both submissions returned 200 and atomically persisted PENDING approval requests tied to the exact simulation ID/checksum; both rules advanced to PENDING_APPROVAL/r3. Reusing the submitter for publish and reject returned deliberate HTTP 422 responses.

items.operation: Approve and publish with an administrator different from both creator and submitter, then reload the real page
items.verificationSql: SELECT r.state,r.revision,a.state,a.revision,a.decided_by,o.event_type,o.topic,o.status,o.attempt_count FROM bpi.bpi_rule_versions r JOIN bpi.bpi_rule_approval_requests a ON a.rule_version_id=r.id LEFT JOIN bpi.bpi_outbox_events o ON o.aggregate_id=r.id WHERE r.id='b54aedc7-6dd2-47cd-fa8e-c95b1a32fefa';
items.evidence: The controlled independent BPI_ADMIN request returned 200. PostgreSQL showed rule PUBLISHED/r4, approval APPROVED/r2 and one BOUNDARY_RULE_PUBLISHED outbox row. The page reload displayed the published state. Outbox remained PENDING with attempts=0 because the Phase 1 target intentionally keeps the dispatcher disabled during this control-plane acceptance.

items.operation: Reject a pending rule with a different administrator and verify return to draft on the real page
items.verificationSql: SELECT r.state,r.revision,a.state,a.revision,a.decided_by,a.decision_reason FROM bpi.bpi_rule_versions r JOIN bpi.bpi_rule_approval_requests a ON a.rule_version_id=r.id WHERE r.id='c1e5ea8e-7d1b-54ef-3a76-d3ab09a2e3bb';
items.evidence: The controlled independent BPI_ADMIN request returned 200. PostgreSQL showed rule DRAFT/r4 and approval REJECTED/r2 with the decision actor/reason; no publication outbox was created. The page reload displayed the rejected rule back in draft.

cleanup.featureFlagPolicy: The shared bpi.rule-management flag was preserved; only the marker actor was normalized to bpi-test-environment.

boundaries: This acceptance proves target control-plane version comparison and rule approval/rejection persistence only.
Phase 1 remains shadow-only and does not write WOM, QCS or WMS production state.
Rule retirement, typed inactive delivery, broker failure, application image rollback and product-level rollback remain separate acceptance work.
